title: The Sobolev bound passes from mollifications to the limit (parent steps 3–4; Simon Ch. 3, 4.3 with Ch. 2, 2.5)
statement: Let P be a natural number and let p > 0 and c ≥ 0 be real numbers. Write L^P = volume on R^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), |Dw| for the operator norm of the derivative and div g = trace Dg. Assume the Sobolev inequality (S): every C¹ function w : R^P → R with compact support satisfies (∫ |w|^p dL^P)^{1/p} ≤ c ∫ |Dw| dL^P. Let u : R^P → R be Lebesgue integrable with compact support, and let M ∈ R satisfy |∫ u div g dL^P| ≤ M for every C¹ compactly supported g : R^P → R^P with |g(z)| ≤ 1 for all z. Let (η_k)_{k∈N} be C¹ functions R^P → R with compact support such that η_k ≥ 0, η_k(−z) = η_k(z) for all z, and ∫ η_k dL^P = 1. Assume (η_k * u)(x) → u(x) as k → ∞ for L^P-a.e. x. Here (η * u)(x) = ∫ η(t) u(x − t) dt is Mathlib's convolution with lsmul ℝ ℝ and volume. Then (∫ |u|^p dL^P)^{1/p} ≤ c M, with Bochner integrals and the power 1/p written p⁻¹.
